question: Using the inverse-matrix method, solve $2x+3y=7$ and $x+2y=4$. Hence, find $x^2+y^2$.
explanation:
Matrix representation
The system can be written as $AX=B$, where $$A=\begin{bmatrix}2&3\\1&2\end{bmatrix},\quad X=\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix},\quad B=\begin{bmatrix}7\\4\end{bmatrix}$$
Inverse of the coefficient matrix
Since $|A|=4-3=1$, $$A^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}2&-3\\-1&2\end{bmatrix}$$
Calculation of the solution matrix
Using $X=A^{-1}B$, $$X=\begin{bmatrix}2&-3\\-1&2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}7\\4\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}14-12\\-7+8\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2\\1\end{bmatrix}$$
Required value
Therefore, $$x^2+y^2=2^2+1^2=5$$
